text:
[IERR.2.8.1] Claimed beyond `-599`:

| Range | Category |
|---|---|
| `-600..-610` | native Rete loader and realtime |
| `-620..-625` | series-backend ABI |
| `-700..-704` | dialect / artefact binding |
| `-710..-714` | realtime contract |
| `-720..-730` | event trace |

Gaps inside a claimed decade are headroom
for that decade's families, not free space for a new one.

Registering an allocation before the code exists is as much
of this clause's job as recording one that already exists.

The reservation is also why this table is read when a
`-6xx` / `-7xx` code is allocated and not only when one is
defined. This clause is named authoritative beyond `-599`
([NERR.3.1]) while the register's **gated** rendering is
`[NERR.13]`, which the error-code gate reconciles against
`libds.h` by NAME. A range row carries no name, so it sits
outside that gate's population entirely: the two
renderings here and in [NERR.3.1] are kept current by
being read, not by being checked.

Compiler diagnostics are **not** in this space and claim
no range here ([RTCT.9.1]). `DS_ERR_` is
the runtime `ds_status_t` prefix; a diagnostic wearing it
is a naming defect, not a band that needs allocating.

`-800` through `-9999` remain reserved for future
categories (debug protocol, observability, TBD). A new
category claims its range by an explicit amendment here, and
this clause is the register that makes the claim real.
